questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That there was a uni with a good level, english courses, nice wheather and close to nature

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Macquaire Uni was very helpful and their whole system works really well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Questions about how to enroll in units as well as how to change units and schedule. I just asked the students administration on campus and called them.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy for me as I knew some people that have been on an exchange in Sydney before and they recommended a shared house so I just texted the owner and asked if there would be space for me. But otherwise most people found housing in FB groups or on Flatmates.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Campus is a bit far from the city and the beach so I would recommend living in the city or near the beach as you only go to school 1-3 times a week. So I spend more time self studying in the library.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing is worse quality in Sydney than in Denmark and at the same time more expensive. Also most housing options are unheated so bring warm clothes. It does get cold in the winther!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Super easy, just follow the guide

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student administration. They have an online portal or on campus office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get "forhåndsgodkendelse" for more subject than you think so you can make sure the schedule doesn't overlap when you then start enrolling in units.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Easier than at KU. However, you have to stay engaged within the whole semester as there are like 3 exams through the semester and not just one at the end but I found that quite nice so the pressure to perform one time isn't so high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Medium. They weren't as critical as we are used to at KU

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Managing change in organisations
Introduction to Human ressource management
Social research methods
Introduction to podcasting

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to podcasting was super fun and a good mix of theory and practice

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't know that OSHI was required so I paid both for that and my own travel insurance so that's why insurance ended up so expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Student visa was like 8500DKK. which was much more than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the dance club but there weren't many people there. In general there were many clubs but not that many people going to them if you think about how many people are at the school

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many sports club, reading, fan clubs and much more

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The running clubs by the beach or in Centanial Park.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go surfing! Run in Centannial, walk the incredible coastal walks, and visit the many beautiful national parks in the area

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, aussies are so open and easy to talk to

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join running clubs for free or join a sport, go to the school parties and live in a shared house

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That people are very nice and easy to talk to but sometimes it's difficult to know ehat they really think and feel and have a deeper connection.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way they take so good care of their beautiful nature and all the "hi" and smiles you get on the street

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate asking for help at the student administration

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's easy to change units of you don't like them

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything can't choose

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not spending all my money lol

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
